_about: Full-episode-only keys for scenarios/awareness_e18_credential_attacks_at_scale/scenario.json.erb. The wiring agent pastes each value into the full erb at the path its note gives. None of these is in the fragment-erb parity comparison (episode-level, or allow-listed erb-only), and the generated defend-only shell never carries them. Authored by opus48. ENG-02 (the guess stage), ENG-02b (the spray/stuff modes), ENG-01 (flipAftermath) and ENG-09b (conceptPanel array) must have landed before the full shell validates; all were confirmed on main (password-guesser-model.js MODE_BUILDERS has spray/stuff; awareness.rb has guess_spray_checks/guess_stuff_checks; test/js/social-password-guesser-spray.test.mjs).

_notes.guess: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.guess (ENG-02 + ENG-02b, mode 'spray'). Episode-level, full-only; dropped from the defend-only shell because `guess` is an ATTACK_STAGES id (episode-model.js stagesFor). mode 'spray' reads roster, wordList, spray, (optional) stuff and passphraseDemo; it must NOT carry target/patternSlots/reuseStep/commonList (awareness.rb guess_spray_checks rejects them). roster.namesFactId, roster.patternFactId and each wordList.slots[].factId name a declared se_intel_* fact (attack.json intelFacts). Each wordList slot's template interpolates ONLY its own {id} token with the slot's own `word` (the made-up string the fact stands for); seasonYear strings are baked literals; tokens never cross slots. spray.passes each carry exactly one of fromSlot (a wordList slot id) or literal (a baked string); spray.opensCount is a whole number not greater than roster.sample length, shown as a count, never a named colleague. stuff.rows are { label, opens } with generic account labels only (no @, : or =, and no password value). landedGlobal (guess_e18_landed) must be a declared global (false). See E18 section 9. P1 F-E18-13/F-E18-12: guess.strings overrides the console's status labels (password-guesser-model.js DEFAULT_TEXT) so they read in plain words: found->collected, opened->opened (not 'opens the account'), trying->'did not open' (settles the held passphrase row), switchOff->'Stop the test' (no 'rig'). The row data-state keys are unchanged, so the bridge's state checks still hold.
_notes.flipAftermath: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.flipAftermath (ENG-01). Episode-level, items authored inline; the runner shows it only when the attack landed (guess_e18_landed true, written by ENG-02b). Re-seats the learner in their own seat as the first alerts arrive, which sets up the defend half. victimName is "you" (the learner's own seat, not a named colleague; the ENG-08 schema requires a string here, so "you" is used rather than the brief's null, matching E9's flipAftermath). The item ids (fa_signin, fa_lockout) are flip-only and are not the defend-set card ids; the scored lockout/sign-in cards are e18_lockout_* and e18_signin_* in defend.json.
_notes.stepLabels: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.stepLabels (ENG-01, reused by ENG-02). Labels the guess step 'Campaign'. The built shells author none, so they are unchanged; optional.
_notes.conceptPanel: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.strings.conceptPanel (ENG-09b array form). IDENTICAL to the value in e18/defend.json awarenessEpisode.strings.conceptPanel: the generator carries that into the defend-only shell too, so all four cards show in both variants. Reproduced here only so the full erb's strings block carries them. conceptPanel is value-exempt and erb-only-OK in the parity allow-list, so no allow-list change is needed.

roster.note: The staff list and address pattern came off the practice's public pages, not from any password.

wordList.note: Candidate passwords built from the practice's own website words plus the season and the year; all made up.

spray.note: One candidate tried once against every account in a pass, so no single account ever locks.

rows.label: A staff wiki login, used nowhere else

stuff.note: A password leaked from another site was tried across many services; the ones that open are where someone reused that password at work.

guess.note: No real password is typed here; every account, word and pair is made up for the exercise.

flipAftermath.heading: A few minutes later, at your desk
flipAftermath.intro: The attack set alarms ringing across the practice. These first two alerts are already in your inbox; you handle the full set next.

items.subject: New sign-in to your account
items.note: An alert about a sign-in; genuine ones send you to the real site, fakes to a look-alike.

items.subject: Some accounts were briefly locked
items.note: The practice locks accounts after a run of bad sign-ins.

flipAftermath.line: Most of the harm comes from acting on the fake alert instead of the real one.

conceptPanel.heading: Password spraying
conceptPanel.text: One likely password, tried just once against every account, so no single account locks. The accounts that open are the predictable ones: a company word, a project name, a season and a year.

conceptPanel.heading: Credential stuffing
conceptPanel.text: A list of address and password pairs stolen from one website, tried automatically across many others. Where someone reused that password at work, the attacker is straight in.

conceptPanel.heading: The one habit
conceptPanel.text: A different password for every account, not a word off the website, kept in a manager, breaks both: the spray has nothing predictable to try, and a stolen pair opens nothing else.

conceptPanel.heading: What the practice does
conceptPanel.text: On the practice's side: accounts lock after a run of bad sign-ins, MFA is on everything, the obvious words are blocked from passwords, and a monitoring partner watches the breach lists for the practice's addresses. These are set up for you; you don't have to switch them on.
